human_readable: U.S. Constitution: Originalist vs. Living Document
summary: KERNEL CONTEST: [ANALYTICAL ESTIMATE] Single fixed substrate: The U.S. Constitution (1787 text + amendments). Reading A (Originalist): Authority grounded in framers' intent/textual meaning at ratification; beneficiaries include states' rights advocates, original meaning proponents; structural focus on limiting judicial expansion. Reading B (Living Constitution): Authority grounded in evolving societal values and contemporary application; beneficiaries include civil rights expansion advocates; structural focus on adaptive interpretation. These readings emit divergent constraints on judicial power, federal-state relations, and individual rights scope.

human_readable: UN Charter: Sovereignty vs. Humanitarian Intervention
summary: KERNEL CONTEST: [ANALYTICAL ESTIMATE] Single fixed substrate: UN Charter Article 2(7) on non-intervention + Chapter VII enforcement powers. Reading A (Sovereignty-first): Authority grounded in state sovereignty as primary principle; beneficiaries include post-colonial states, authoritarian regimes; structural focus on blocking external interference. Reading B (Responsibility to Protect): Authority grounded in universal human rights obligations; beneficiaries include populations under persecution; structural focus on legitimizing intervention. These readings produce divergent constraints on military action, diplomatic pressure, and accountability mechanisms.

human_readable: Islamic Law: Classical Sharia vs. Reformist Interpretations
summary: KERNEL CONTEST: [ANALYTICAL ESTIMATE] Single fixed substrate: Quran + Hadith corpus. Reading A (Traditionalist): Authority grounded in classical fiqh schools and historical consensus; beneficiaries include traditional religious authorities; structural focus on preserving established jurisprudence. Reading B (Reformist/Ijtihad): Authority grounded in contextual reinterpretation for modern circumstances; beneficiaries include progressive Muslims, women's rights advocates; structural focus on adapting rulings to contemporary ethics. These readings emit divergent constraints on gender roles, criminal justice, and religious authority structures.

human_readable: Declaration of Independence: 'All Men Created Equal'
summary: KERNEL CONTEST: [ANALYTICAL ESTIMATE] Single fixed substrate: Declaration of Independence (1776), 'all men are created equal.' Reading A (Restrictive original): Authority grounded in 18th-century property-owning male citizens; beneficiaries include founding generation elites; structural focus on limited franchise, property rights. Reading B (Expansive universal): Authority grounded in universal human equality transcending historical context; beneficiaries include marginalized groups, civil rights movements; structural focus on expanding rights beyond original scope. These readings emit divergent constraints on voting rights, anti-discrimination law, and social welfare policy.

human_readable: WTO Agreements: Development vs. Market Access
summary: KERNEL CONTEST: [ANALYTICAL ESTIMATE] Single fixed substrate: WTO agreements (GATT, TRIPS, TRIMS). Reading A (Market liberalization): Authority grounded in free trade principles, comparative advantage; beneficiaries include multinational corporations, export-oriented economies; structural focus on reducing barriers. Reading B (Developmental special treatment): Authority grounded in special and differential treatment for developing nations; beneficiaries include Global South countries, infant industries; structural focus on protective measures, technology transfer. These readings produce divergent constraints on tariffs, intellectual property, and industrial policy space.
